text:
sam: Heads-up — seeing intermittent 150–300ms tail spikes on small chat requests after the kernel switch. Pattern looks like short microbursts that fail to coalesce.

jia: timeline? which kernel + config did we change?

sam: canary rolled flash-attn2 last night (build r-2026.04.02). Runtime microbatch target moved from 4ms -> 2ms to reduce p50. coalesce_delay was 6ms, jitter +/-2ms. now effective hold is ~1.2ms in practice.

noah: got logs? any KV cache churn at the same time?

sam: attaching quick profiler snippet from one spike window:

```
perf_summary:
  p50: 11ms
  p95: 84ms
  p99: 228ms
hotspots:
  - kernel: flash-attn2
    time_ratio: 0.58
  - runtime: batch_formation.wait
    avg_wait: 2.1ms
  - kv_cache.lookup
    miss_rate: 7.3%  # higher than baseline
```

ashley: kv miss rate jump is suspicious — are we invalidating prefixes when microbatches move differently?

sam: hypothesis: tighter interval reduces chance to combine arrivals; we then hit kernel entry/exit overhead more often, plus KV priming races. observed more small batch kernels (<4 tokens) which are inefficient for flash-attn2.

jia: suggestion: revert microbatch target to 3ms and increase coalesce_delay to 7ms for canary, keep jitter but widen to +/-3ms. quick A/B.

noah: also try forcing kernel fallback for small-token batches (threshold 8 tokens) to old-attn optimized path. If flash-attn2 has per-call setup cost, avoiding it for tiny batches could help.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: rollback-microtarget-3ms (canary) started by jia at 1948765600

sam: ran a short A/B on two canary nodes:
- node A (3ms target / 7ms delay / jitter +/-3ms): p99 ~ 120ms
- node B (2ms target / 6ms delay / jitter +/-2ms): p99 ~ 220ms

noah: big delta. can you paste sample batch-size histogram?

sam: histogram (counts over 10k requests):
```
batch_size_bins: [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8+]
nodeA_counts: [420, 1100, 2100, 2600, 1800, 900, 500, 580]
nodeB_counts: [950, 1800, 2700, 2000, 900, 350, 150, 250]
```

ashley: nodeB has many more 1-2 token batches -> aligns with tail spike. KV warmups wasted.

jia: for short-term mitigation: widen jitter and coalesce delay, and add a microbatch floor: hold at least 2.5ms minimum before dispatching single-token requests unless queue length > N. (N=8?)

noah: we should be careful: holding single-token requests increases median; we want to reduce p99 while keeping p50 acceptable. propose policy:
- dynamic hold: if queue_recent_rate < threshold then hold to coalesce, else dispatch.
- per-model token-budget target: favor coalesce for small token requests under 12 tokens.

sam: implemented a quick runtime flag: `micro_min_hold_ms=2.5`, `coalesce_delay_ms=7`, `jitter_ms=3`, and `small_batch_kernel_threshold=8`.

perf-bot: perf report uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/7821 (summary: canary nodes show p99 improved 45%)

ashley: important to monitor KV eviction activity — we saw priming causing spikes when we switch kernel path (different KV access patterns). add kv_hit_rate, kv_eviction_rate to rollout dashboard.

jia: also add a kernel-selection metric: %calls_to_flash_attn2_by_batch_size. we need to verify flash-attn2 only when it's net-positive.

noah: longer-term: consider cost model in router: route tiny requests to a lightweight CPU-optimized path or a cached response tier if available.

sam: one other oddity — when multiple tiny batches hit same sequence prefix, KV lookup latency increases due to lock contention. switching to lock-free read path for read-only KV ops reduced tail in tests.

jia: action items:
- revert canary globally to nodeA config for 24h (jia)
- add kernel-selection fallback rule by batch size (noah)
- dashboard kv and kernel metrics (ashley)
- prototype lock-free KV read fastpath (sam)

ashley: I'll wire alarms for kv_eviction_rate > 1% and flash_attn2_p99 > 200ms.

ops-bot: canary rollback completed at 1948765780

sam: thanks. will follow up with a short write-up and perf graphs tomorrow. :thumbsup:

jia: great investigation — this is a good example of interaction between batching heuristics and kernel microbench characteristics. keep notes for postmortem.

noah: agreed. nice triage team. :clap:
